commentary_segments.text: A differential version of the single-transistor Pierce oscillator is shown in this slide. For low frequencies, the impedance of the capacitor C is too large and no oscillation can build up. At high frequencies, it acts as a short and a negative impedance is presented to the crystal. The resistors have to be sufficiently high not to dampen the oscillation. They are better when replaced by current sources. The current setting sources I are better driven by an AGC loop, which measures the output B voltages. If not, the currents may be set too high, resulting in larger deviations in frequency or distortion.

If not, the currents may be set too high, resulting in larger deviations in frequency or distortion.
